title: Heading to New Orleans in 1932: Ben Pollack band and Bourbon Street
summary: Kelly recounts the Depression, hearing the Ben Pollack band, the Studio Club and Silver Slipper, and getting a job offer with Mr. LaCoste.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Okay. There was a music store in 3-4th, formed by Bubba Broyles. Bubba was a trumpet player, and he'd been playing with the local bands there. And, he was a great friend of Mr. A.J. LaCoste, who was a power with the Whirland Organization. A.J. was the management of the band department. He organized school bands all over Mississippi and Louisiana. He was a tremendous man. But, Bubba and LaCoste asked me to come to New Orleans, that I would have some kind of a job. I had, I tried to go back to playing and played with Dick Richardson's band out of Dallas and played with numerous bands, but there wasn't any work. I guess it was in 1930, the bottom. Well, I didn't even tell you if I found my own band. I took a wonderful band out on the road in 1930. Of all times, we would take a band on the road. I took them out in 1930. And, among them were some of the classical musicians in the whole country. And, so, let's see, where have we found here? Well, anyway, my little band had broken up. And, I was supposed to go to work for a group in Shreveport who were playing at the radio station. Well, when I got over there, there was a young kid playing the old fellow who was working his way through school. And, he was a good saxophone player. And, so, I didn't want to bump him up. The guys that asked me to come over, but when I got there, it didn't seem a comfortable thing to do. So, there I was, but I ate jobs. So, I was hanging around Bubba's music store. He said, I'll get you a job in New Orleans. So, I went on to New Orleans in 1932. And, that is the year that the Ben Pollack Band played Club Forrest in New Orleans. And, Aidy Miller had just joined the band. And, of course, Jack G. Gardner and all of the, what later became the Fosby Band. They were Prince Preet. Stirling Bowles was with them. Jack was with them. Matt and Matt Rock was with them. Ray Badoop was with them. Natty Lamar was with them. All of these guys. And, I went out to hear them. And, it was great. And, I'll never forget that the night that I was there, we went to the Studio Club. At that time, there were just two clubs on Bourbon Street. One was the Studio Club and one was the Silver Slipper. Sharky was playing Silver Slipper and had a little band at the Studio Club with Pat De Queer. And, that was where I posed in and numerous other guys. Bob Fryberger, who you probably have never heard of, but he was a Yankee. Great Trombone player who was there. And, so, on that trip, I had an interview with Mr. McCausse. Mr. McCausse said, okay, come on down. I'll put you on a commission basis. And, you can play on the side of the mic. So, I came back to the Streetport and I had a little Pontiac, a Port Caballet.
